# Macro regime fixtures — historical regression tests

Generated by `scripts/_emit_macro_regime_fixtures.ts`. Each `.csv` here freezes
the inputs (VIX/VIX3M/HYG/SPY closes + S&P 500 %-above-50DMA breadth) for a
named historical window so the classifier produces the same regime sequence on
every CI run.

The CSVs are **derived from real market data** ingested into ClickHouse via
`npm run macro:ingest`. They are NOT hand-curated — fabricating fixture values
would silently tune the implementation to its own tests (Bergstra-Bengio 2012;
Aronson 2006 §6 hypothesis-testing-on-test-data anti-pattern).

## Fixtures (SPEC §5.2)

| File                              | Window                  | Expectation |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------- | --- |
| `2008_gfc.csv`                    | 2008-08-01 → 2009-03-31 | sustained red across most days |
| `2011_eu_debt.csv`                | 2011-07-01 → 2011-10-31 | orange/red in August |
| `2014_calm.csv`                   | 2014-04-01 → 2014-09-30 | majority green; no red |
| `2018_q4_selloff.csv`             | 2018-09-01 → 2018-12-31 | yellow → orange in October |
| `2020_covid.csv`                  | 2020-02-19 → 2020-04-30 | red within ~5 days of 2020-02-24 |
| `2017_holdout.csv`                | 2017-01-03 → 2017-12-29 | distribution recorded only — NO threshold tuning |

**The 2017 holdout is calibration-immune.** It is run last, its regime
distribution is reported, and no parameter is touched in response. This is
the closest thing to out-of-sample we get with 5 calibrated regimes plus
1 holdout (SPEC §5.2).

## CSV format

```
trade_date,vix_close,vix3m_close,hyg_close,spy_close,pct_above_50dma,breadth_source
2008-08-01,22.57,24.10,93.20,128.34,42.0,stooq_a50r
...
```

Empty cells = data missing for that day. The classifier's NULL-input rules
fire (`inputs_missing` bitmask). Do not interpolate or backfill.

## Regenerating

After a successful `npm run macro:ingest` populates the relevant range, run:

```
npx tsx scripts/_emit_macro_regime_fixtures.ts
```

This writes (or overwrites) the six CSV files. Commit the changes; CI will
then exercise the historical-regression layer of the test suite.

## Why the test suite passes when fixtures are absent

`macroRegimeFixtures.test.ts` skips a fixture's assertions when its CSV is
missing — first-time-bootstrap doesn't fail CI just because nobody has run
the emitter yet. Once a fixture is committed, the test enforces the regime
distribution every run thereafter. Add new fixtures only by running the
emitter; do not hand-edit CSVs.
